question: Name India's oldest nuclear reactor which was recommissioned in 2018.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Apsara**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• I**ndia's oldest nuclear reactor, Apsara, was recommissioned in 2018** as an upgraded version called Apsara-Upgraded
 
• **Apsara**
 
 
• **The first research reactor in Asia, Apsara was operational in 1956** at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC) in Trombay.
 
• It was a **pool-type reacto**r that used highly enriched uranium as fuel and light water as both a moderator and coolant.
 
• After providing service for over five decades, it was shut down in 2009.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhaskar**

 
 
• It refers to **India’s Bhaskara satellites**, launched in the late 1970s and early 1980s by ISRO for Earth observation.
 
• These **satellites focused on remote sensing applications**, including forestry, hydrology, and geology.
 
• It is Designed primarily for **remote sensing applications**.
 
 
 
• **Dhanush**
 
 
• **​**Dhanush is a **ship-based, short-range ballistic missile system** developed by India’s Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO).
 
• It is a naval variant of the **Prithvi missile** and is capable of launching nuclear and conventional payloads.
 
 
 
• **Dhruva**
 
 
• **​**Dhruva is a **nuclear research reactor, also located at the Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (BARC), Mumbai.**
 
• It was **commissioned in 1985**, making it much newer than Apsara.
 
• Dhruva is** India's largest research reactor, **mainly used for producing radioisotopes for medical and industrial purposes and for conducting research in nuclear physics and material science.
